request.prompt:

DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

agent.result_text:
The rollover change is done, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests in the spec on two runs in a row.

**The change** (`PeriodService.java`): after a rollover writes its `ROLLOVER` audit line, it soft-closes each period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in start-date order. A period that is already closed or soft-closed is skipped, so in the main test the closed 2026-11 period gets no line. Each soft-close goes through the same code as a soft-close by hand: it fixes the period's figures and cuts and writes a `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED … period=… total=…` line. To share that code I moved the body of `softClose` into a private `softCloseNow` helper.

Two choices you may want to revisit:
- **Permission:** rollover already requires a steward, so it doesn't also check the sheet's close permission before these soft-closes.
- **Undo:** undoing a rollover does not reopen the periods it soft-closed. The request didn't cover undo and none of the tests use it.

**A second fix outside the request:** on the first run, scenario 3 failed. It doesn't use rollover. When the sheet is viewed as of a past date, the crews list ignored that date and showed today's members. So a crew Cam had since been merged out of showed shares of 50.00 instead of 33.34. I changed `CrewController.java` to build the crews from the sheet's history when an as-of date is given, the same way the people list already does. After that, every run passed.
